₹1 crore, zero equity, and you don't need to be based in Karnataka to apply. Twenty days left.

ELEVATE NxT 2026–27 is the deep-tech track of Karnataka's flagship startup grant, run by Startup Karnataka under the state's Department of Electronics, IT, BT and S&T. Selected startups receive an equity-free grant-in-aid of up to ₹1 crore, released in milestone-linked tranches, along with incubation and mentoring links across Karnataka's government-backed startup network.

The call is aimed at genuine deep-tech products between Technology Readiness Level 3 and 8, across areas such as AI, robotics, biotech, semiconductors, space and advanced manufacturing. You can apply as a private limited company, LLP, registered partnership or cooperative society incorporated within the last 20 years, with turnover below ₹300 crore in every year and at least two founding or core team members. Subsidiaries and spin-offs are not eligible, and past ELEVATE winners from the previous three years are excluded.

The catch many founders miss: if you win and your company is registered outside Karnataka, you must move your registered office to the state within four months of the results. You also have to submit a short write-up justifying why your product counts as deep tech, so prepare it carefully.

Most biotech founders think ₹1 crore of non-dilutive money only comes once or twice a year. This one reviews proposals every month.

C-CAMP, the Bengaluru life-sciences hub, runs the Wadhwani Innovation Network Centre of Excellence with the Wadhwani Foundation. Through this standing call, it gives up to ₹1 crore of non-dilutive funding to Indian startups and academic innovators who need to take a technology beyond TRL 4. The money can go into pilot and validation studies, prototype refinement and scale-up work, the kind of evidence that makes your next fundraise far easier.

It is open to products and processes, not services, in healthcare, drugs, medical devices, diagnostics, industrial biotechnology and agriculture. Your technology should already be past TRL 4, be novel with IP potential, and come with a clear commercialisation plan. Reviewers also look for a team that combines technical and business skills, with a real grasp of end users and market size.

A practical tip: proposals need to reach C-CAMP before the 20th of a month to enter that month's cycle, so the next cut-off is 20 December 2026. The page doesn't spell out project duration, IP or royalty terms, so email the WIN CoE team to clarify these before you apply.

Paying a patent attorney out of pocket? If you are a DPIIT-recognised startup, the Government of India will cover that fee for you.

The Startups Intellectual Property Protection scheme, known as SIPP, is run by DPIIT under Startup India together with the Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks. It lets startups file patents, trademarks and industrial designs through empanelled facilitators whose professional charges are paid by the government, for any number of filings. On top of that, startups pay 80% less than other companies on patent filing fees, get a 50% rebate on trademark filing fees, and can opt for expedited examination so a patent is granted sooner.

To use it, you need DPIIT recognition under the Startup India framework, and the filing must be for a patent, trademark or design in India routed through one of the listed facilitators. There is no application window; it is an always-on benefit you can use at any stage, from idea to growth.

One catch to watch: only the facilitator's professional fee is covered. The reduced statutory government fees are still yours to pay, and some facilitators quote extra services such as prior-art searches separately, so ask for a clear quote up front.
